gruss_morgen.text: The early bird catches the... muck. I mean... well, you know. Good morning, chick!

gruss_tag.text: Well, chick? The stable won't sweep itself. I tried. Three times.

gruss_abend.text: Evening light! The horses are already snoring. One of them whistles the ranch anthem while doing it.

gruss_regen.text: Get in here! Nobody chases a Gooby out the door in this weather. The horses love it, by the way.

gruss_freund.text: Ah, my favorite chick! Come here, the coffee in the trough is always warm for you.

optionen.text: Tell me about the old days!

text: Remember one thing: a clean stable is half the victory.
The other half is hay. So strictly speaking, everything is hay.
You're coming along, chick. The horses already turn their ears when you show up.
They usually only do that for me. And for the feed cart. Fine, mostly for the feed cart.
You know, I don't say this often: without you this farm would still be a pile of planks with an attitude.
Don't spread it around. I have a reputation as a tough nut to protect.

quest_vergabe.text: I've got something. Nothing wild — unless it goes wrong, then it gets wild.

quest_annahme.text: That's what I like! Chop chop — and don't you dare do it better than me.

ablehnung.text: No drama. The muck won't run away. That's the beautiful and the sad thing about muck.

quest_abgabe.text: Well, look at that! Clean work, chick. Here, hold out your hooves.

geschenk_liebt.text: An apple?! For ME? Chick, now I'm going soft. Tell no one.

geschenk_mag.text: Oh, thank you! This is not going into the feed trough. Half of it, at most.

geschenk_normal.text: Hm. It's the thought that counts. The thought is counting very, very loudly right now.

text: The old days? There was nothing here. Just me, a bucket and a pony named Bruno.
Bruno ate the bucket. That's when I knew: this is going to be a good farm.
The headscarf? It was my grandma's. She weathered the great storm of her day with it.
It wasn't the scarf that helped. But grandma looked fantastic wearing it, and that's what matters.
Now you know. If you tell anyone, I'm afraid I'll have to adopt you.

tschuess.text: Off you go, chick! And remember: the horse comes first, then the fun. Usually they're the same thing.
